The test image shows a corn ear with:
- Bleached/white husks
- White cottony mold material on the ear tip/kernels
- Severely dead/gray-brown dry plant tissue surrounding the ear

This pattern — bleached husks with white mold — points toward Ear_rots_Diplodia or possibly Fusarium. Let me check reference images.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Corn ear with prominently **bleached/white husks**
- White cottony mold material visible on the exposed kernels at the tip
- Entire surrounding plant is completely dead, dry, gray-brown
- Kernels appear white/cream colored (possible white mold covering)

**Candidate elimination:**
- **Gibberella**: ruled out — no pink/red mold
- **Aspergillus**: ruled out — no olive-green powdery mold
- **Trichoderma**: ruled out — no dark green mold
- **Fusarium**: less likely — no starburst pattern, no scattered pink/salmon mold on yellow kernels

**Why Ear_rots_Diplodia:**
The **bleached husks** are the single most diagnostic feature of Diplodia ear rot. The Diplodia reference collage showed exactly this pattern — bleached papery white husks with the dead plant backdrop and white fungal mycelium over the kernels. The white mold on the ear tip/kernels also matches. While the description mentions "while the rest of the plant remains green," late-season infection can result in the completely dead/dry plant seen here.
